trace.title: Reactive source
trace.detail: reactive returns a proxy. Vue can track property reads through that proxy and notify effects when relevant writes happen. ref creates a reactive value wrapper. JavaScript uses .value; templates unwrap refs in supported contexts.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Read query inside computed → Vue records that dependency. Change query → computed becomes stale → a dependent render asks for the new value. Several synchronous writes can lead to one DOM update batch.

Use shallowRef when you intentionally treat a large outside object as one replaceable value. Deep mutation will not behave like an ordinary deep reactive ref. Choose it for a reason, such as an external editor instance, not as a universal speed switch.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Watching a computed merely to copy it into another ref creates two sources. Mutating a raw object behind a proxy can bypass the access path you expected Vue to track.
